title: Geometry of Living — Faith, Belief, Philosophy, and Civilizational Generative Priors
subtitle: A Comparative Systems-Theoretic Interpretation within the PoLPEST Framework

blocks.text: This chapter presents the poster “Geometry of Living — Faith, Belief, Philosophy, and Civilizational Generative Priors” in full. It is a single dense diagram; open it, then use the explanation, read-aloud, and Ask-AI tools beneath it to work through the ideas at your own pace.

blocks.explanation: A comparative, systems-theoretic reading in which belief systems, philosophical traditions, skepticism, historical texts, and scientific thought are interpreted as high-level generative models shaping cognition and collective organization — explicitly distinguished as speculative synthesis, not established scholarship. Belief functions as a generative prior; organized religions as large-scale shared generative models; skepticism and atheism as continual model revision. Classical strategic and ethical texts (Bhagavad Gita, Nahj al-Balagha, The Art of War, Analects, Arthashastra) and modern thinkers are located as different regions of a conceptual landscape, and each of religion, skepticism, philosophy, and science is assigned a functional role within the PoLPEST framework.
blocks.tts: Faith, belief, philosophy, and science as generative priors: a comparative systems-theoretic interpretation, presented as research proposal rather than settled consensus.
